title: Constraint-aware multimode canary planner with rollback simulation
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Problem: We need a single canary planner that can express and enforce environment-specific constraints (network egress, KMS availability, RBAC scopes, allowed kernel/quantization variants) for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Current rollout logic assumes parity across environments which leads to failed canaries or silent misconfigurations when promoting models to Dedicated/Private tenants.

Goal: Build a constraint-aware multimode canary planner + preflight simulator that: (1) consumes a target rollout manifest and environment capability profile, (2) computes an environment-safe deployment plan (traffic percentages, shadowing, staged promotion), (3) simulates rollback scenarios using historical telemetry to validate automatic rollback thresholds, and (4) emits deterministic translation rules for private deployments (no external callbacks, restricted images, KMS mapping).

Scope: planner service + simulator + small Console UI to review computed plan. Does NOT include full rollout execution engine (we will integrate with the orchestration controller in a follow-up). Must surface clear alarms and runbook links when a promotion is unsafe.

Key constraints: Private environments may lack outbound access, so any canary step that depends on external evaluation services must be expressed as a shadow-only step. Dedicated pools have stricter kernel/quantization compatibility; planner must record a compatible model variant selection. Hosted can use full telemetry-based auto-rollback.

Success criteria / acceptance criteria are listed below.
acceptance_criteria: Planner can ingest environment capability profiles for Hosted, Dedicated, Private
Planner produces a concrete rollout plan (percentages, durations, monitoring gates) for each environment
Simulator runs using sampled historical telemetry and returns pass/fail and suggested rollback thresholds
Translation rules include an explicit 'no-external-callbacks' variant for Private and a compatible-model-variant hint for Dedicated
Console view shows plan summary and simulator output; reviewers can approve or request changes
Integration tests validate that a plan marked 'Private-safe' contains zero external evaluation steps and explicit KMS alias mapping
comments: 2026-02-28 - Triage by Asha: scoped to planner+simulator+review UI. Split execution/integration with controller into follow-up tickets.

2026-03-02 - Engineering design review (Diego, Lina, Omar): opted for a capability-profile approach rather than ad-hoc flags. Trade-off: capability profiles require per-tenant onboarding but simplify reasoning and simulations.
2026-03-04 - UX sync (Kara): Console will show a two-column diff (planned vs environment-adjusted plan) and a toggle to view simulator projections. Follow-up: mockups uploaded to Confluence.

2026-03-05 - Security note (Priya): Private mode must never include external webhook steps; added security gate in simulator to fail preflight if any external steps are present. Security review requested.
2026-03-06 - Implementation update (Diego): implemented capability profile schema prototype and basic planner algorithm. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3421
2026-03-08 - QA: added synthetic telemetry harness to feed simulator. Early runs show the planner recommends 'shadow' for an evaluation step when target tenant has no egress.
2026-03-09 - PM feedback (Lina Chen): require explicit annotation for quality-eval vs perf-eval so Private tenants can opt into local evals. Added as follow-up subtask.
2026-03-10 - Risk review: noted potential for alert fatigue if simulator thresholds are set too tight. Plan to surface suggested thresholds and allow reviewers to accept/adjust before execution.
notes: Trade-offs: we chose capability profiles to avoid proliferating boolean flags. Profile onboarding is manual initially but can be automated via a capability discovery agent later.

Quality measurement: simulator supports plugging in offline evals (prompt-based) and perf regressions (p50/p95 latency + token cost delta). Both feed into an aggregate risk score used by the rollback simulator.

Rollout plan template: start 1% hosted internal traffic for 30 mins -> 5% hosted external 1h -> 5% dedicated shadow for 2h -> 10% dedicated canary (if dedicated-compatible) -> promote. Private steps default to shadow-only unless tenant opts into local evals.
Auto-rollback triggers: error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute OR p95 latency regression > 30% OR eval-quality drop > 2% (suggested defaults—simulator will recommend tuned thresholds per workload).
implementation_tasks: schema: capability_profile v1 (network, kms, kernels, quantization, eval_modes)
planner: rule engine to map rollout manifest -> environment-safe plan
simulator: replay engine that consumes historical telemetry and evaluates rollback probability
console: plan explorer and simulator result UI
tests: unit for rule engine, integration using synthetic telemetry harness
docs: onboarding guide for tenant capability profiles and preflight runbook
